releases.notes:
## Sell Allowlist — decide exactly what may be sold

New **Use Allowlist** setting (on by default): the mod only sells items you have allowlisted. Everything else stays in your inventory — it is never moved, and it never blocks a sell cycle. Turning the toggle off sells everything, as before.

Out of the box the allowlist contains five starter items: `minecraft:dandelion`, `minecraft:poppy`, `minecraft:pumpkin`, `minecraft:melon_seeds`, `minecraft:melon_slice`.

### The item picker

Open your settings (`O` or Mod Menu) and click **Edit Allowlist…**:

- Every registered item with its 3D icon, searchable via **fuzzy search** — try `melon sed`, `drk` or `popy`; matches against item names and ids, word order doesn't matter, best matches rank first.
- Click a row to toggle it: green box + check + tint = will be sold; hollow box + dim text = won't.
- Hover a row for its full id and sell status; live counters show your selection size and the filtered item count.
- **All / None** act on the current search results; scroll with the wheel or drag the scrollbar.
- **Done** saves (your list is stored sorted), **Cancel/Esc** discards.

### Notes

- The allowlist is matched by item id (`minecraft:poppy`), so all variants of an item are treated the same.
- If you upgrade from 2.2.x: your existing settings carry over untouched; the allowlist starts with the five defaults and the toggle starts ON.
- Safety rules unchanged: non-allowlisted items are never clicked or moved, armor/offhand are still excluded, and nothing is ever dropped.

releases.notes:
## Fixed

**Toggling auto-sell off and on again while the sell GUI is open now resumes selling in that same GUI.** Previously the mod would idle after re-enabling (it never sends the sell command while a screen is open, and it had forgotten that the open GUI was the sell GUI) until you closed and let it reopen the GUI.

Safety unchanged: the GUI's identity is preserved across the toggle only while that exact screen stays open — a different chest you opened in the meantime is never touched, and closing the GUI clears the memory for good.

releases.notes:
## What's new

### The toggle keybind now works inside GUIs

Pressing `K` (or whatever you bound it to) now toggles auto-sell **everywhere** — including inside the sell GUI, which previously swallowed the key. Details:

- Works in any screen; skipped only while you are typing in chat, a book, a sign or a report field, and in the vanilla Controls screen (so the key can still be rebound there).
- A held key produces exactly one toggle (press/repeat discrimination), and the press is consumed so the GUI never also acts on it.

### Update check

When you join a multiplayer server, the mod asks GitHub once whether a newer release exists and, if so, shows a chat message with a **clickable link** to that release (hovering shows the URL). This single request is the mod's only network traffic besides the Minecraft connection: asynchronous (never blocks the game), 5 s timeout, no retries, completely silent on errors, skipped in singleplayer, and can be turned off in the settings under **Updates → Check for Updates on Join**.

### Fixed

- The settings screen's *reset* button for **Sell Mode** now correctly restores **Keep Open** (it used to reset to Close GUI, contradicting the actual default).

releases.notes:
## Never-fail recovery: no crashes, no giving up — ever

This release rebuilds the failure handling so the mod keeps selling through anything a high-ping connection (or a flaky server) throws at it. Nothing can crash the client and, while you are connected, the mod never turns itself off — it retries, reopens, and recovers, indefinitely.

### It never crashes

- Every slot click is bounds- and null-checked before it reaches vanilla (an out-of-range slot in the client's local click prediction would otherwise throw).
- The whole state machine runs inside a catch-all: if some unexpected vanilla interaction ever throws, the current cycle resets, the error is logged (throttled to once per 30 s), and selling continues on the next tick.

### It never gives up (while connected)

- Sell GUI did not open? Retried forever with a capped backoff: 5 s → 10 s → 20 s → 30 s between attempts.
- GUI closed or replaced mid-cycle? Short cooldown, then a fresh cycle — reopening the GUI and depositing again.
- GUI full? The button gets extra clicks, then the GUI is closed and reopened to flush it (sells-on-close servers) — the pre-existing behavior, now joined by:
- Sell button only picks items up? Escalates to the same close-and-reopen recovery instead of ever disabling.
- Cursor holds an item and your inventory is full? The stack is parked in an empty sell-GUI slot (sold with the rest). Nothing free anywhere (possible while the server still owes confirmations on a high-ping link)? It waits and retries — a GUI is **never** closed while the cursor holds an item, so nothing can ever be dropped.
- Disconnected? The cycle resets but the toggle stays: selling resumes automatically on your next server join. Press `K` to stop — a manual stop stays off.

### High-ping tolerance

- Button clicks get a full second of grace before a loaded cursor is counted as a real pickup.
- The sell GUI may take up to 5 s to appear when the **GUI Title Check** is enabled (the exact title proves it is the command's response). With the check off the acceptance window stays at 1 s so a chest you open yourself is never hijacked — enable the title check on high-ping connections.

### Notes

- Behavior change: auto-sell now survives disconnects and resumes on join (previously it turned itself off). Toggle off with `K` if you do not want that.
- On a server without a sell GUI the mod keeps retrying the sell command (one message per attempt, backoff-capped) until toggled off.
- All packet-level safety guarantees are unchanged: only vanilla client methods, byte-identical to manual play (see docs/PROTOCOL-AUDIT.md).
